lines.text: They dug up a ten-foot stone man in eighteen sixty-nine.
But somebody had buried the giant there on purpose.
A cigar maker named George Hull
argued with a preacher about giants in the Bible.
So Hull decided to make one.
He had a huge block of stone cut in Iowa,
and a sculptor carved it into a giant.
Then he buried it on a farm in Cardiff,
Until diggers finally hit the stone foot.
And the whole town went wild.
People paid twenty-five cents to see him.
But experts called him a fake.
Even the showman P. T. Barnum built his own copy.
Then Hull confessed. The giant was a hoax.
Today he is still on display in Cooperstown.
Would you have paid to see the giant?
